what_its_for: Irinotecan is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of cancer, most commonly colorectal cancer (cancer of the colon or rectum). It may also be used for other cancers such as pancreatic cancer. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_to_take: Irinotecan is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into your vein by a nurse or doctor at a clinic or hospital. You will NOT take this medicine at home by mouth. Each infusion usually takes about 90 minutes. You may be given other medicines before your infusion to help prevent nausea and diarrhea, so arrive a little early for your appointments. Do not miss your scheduled infusion appointments — they are very important for your treatment to work.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose based on your body size (height and weight), your type of cancer, and how well your body handles the medicine. Irinotecan is typically given once every 1 to 3 weeks depending on your treatment plan. Your dose may be adjusted or temporarily stopped if you experience serious side effects. Never try to change your dose on your own — always talk to your cancer care team first.
missed_dose: Since irinotecan is given by healthcare professionals at a clinic or hospital, it is very important that you keep all of your scheduled appointments. If you need to reschedule or miss an appointment, call your doctor or cancer center as soon as possible. Do not try to make up a missed infusion on your own — your doctor will decide the best plan for you.
storage: You do not need to store irinotecan at home, as it is prepared and given to you by healthcare professionals. If for any reason you are given supplies to take home, keep them away from children and pets, store them as directed by your pharmacist or nurse, and dispose of any unused medicine safely according to your care team's instructions.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking new medicines — including vitamins, herbal supplements, and over-the-counter drugs — without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many can interact with irinotecan. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) completely, as it can make irinotecan less effective. Avoid people who are sick with infections, as chemotherapy can weaken your immune system. Do not receive live vaccines (such as live flu vaccine) during treatment without asking your doctor first. Avoid alcohol or limit it, as it may worsen nausea. Do not become pregnant or father a child during treatment — use reliable birth control, as irinotecan can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room RIGHT AWAY if you experience: severe diarrhea (more than 4 loose stools per day or any watery diarrhea), diarrhea that starts within 24 hours of your infusion along with stomach cramps or sweating, fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, signs of infection such as chills, sore throat, or burning with urination, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe nausea or vomiting that prevents you from eating or drinking, difficulty breathing or chest pain, severe stomach pain or cramping, signs of dehydration such as dizziness, very dark urine, or dry mouth, or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Do not wait — diarrhea from irinotecan can become life-threatening very quickly if not treated.
when_it_works: Irinotecan starts working right away inside your body, but it may take several weeks or months of treatment before you or your doctor can measure how well it is controlling your cancer. Your doctor will check your progress with regular blood tests, scans, and checkups. It is important to continue all scheduled treatments and follow-up visits even if you feel okay.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older) may be more sensitive to side effects such as diarrhea and low blood cell counts and should be monitored closely. Patients with liver problems or a condition called Gilbert's syndrome (a harmless liver condition where bilirubin levels are slightly elevated) may have a higher risk of serious side effects and may need a lower dose. Irinotecan should NOT be used during pregnancy as it can harm the unborn baby — women of childbearing age must use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after. Breastfeeding is not recommended during irinotecan treatment. Talk to your doctor if any of these situations apply to you.
